jobs.description: For our location in Zeuthen we are seeking:Postdoc on IceCube-Gen2Remuneration Group 13 | Limited: 2 years | Start: no later than 01.09.2027 | ID: APPO004/2026 | Deadline: 03.01.2027 | Full-time/Part-timeDESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.The IceCube Neutrino Observatory instruments a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice at the South Pole and discovered the flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. In early 2026, the IceCube Upgrade was completed. IceCube-Gen2 is the next step: an observatory that will be about an order of magnitude larger than IceCube, built to identify the sources of cosmic neutrinos and open new windows on the high-energy universe. The project is being prioritzed by the German goverment, and development work is well under way. DESY thereby has a major role in the design and construction of the detector.DESY is looking for a postdoctoral researcher to help develop the optical sensors of IceCube-Gen2, the next-generation neutrino observatory at the South Pole. You will help build and test the light sensors for IceCube-Gen2, working closely with our engineers and technicians.About your role:- Test new light sensors (photomultipliers) and organize the parts for their electronics, together with our electronics workshop.- Help integrate the sensors into the detector modules, together with our mechanical engineers.- Use simulations to compare sensor designs and their effect on detector performanceIn addition, you will be supported in developing your own research programme within the wide range of activities of our neutrino group, from IceCube data analysis and multimessenger astronomy to physics studies for IceCube-Gen2.About you:- PhD in physics, astronomy or an equivalent qualification- Experience in data analysis in high-energy physics, astroparticle physics or astronomy- Experience developing and/or testing scientific instrumentation for particle or astroparticle physics experiments- Software development skills in Python or C++- Very good command of English- Enjoyment of working in a diverse team of scientists and engineers, and willingness to travel internationallyGood reasons to join:Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. Respectful cooperation and the well-being of our staff are central to us, with gender equality forming a key part of this commitment. To support work life balance we offer flexible working hours and variable part-time. You will benefit from our family-friendly and collegial atmosphere, our established health management and occupational pension provision. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. The pay grade for this position depends on the candidate’s qualifications and assigned duties, up to the above-mentioned remuneration group, in accordance with TV-AVH (https://www.av-hamburg.de/tarifvertraege/#c1886) regulations and the TVöD Bund (https://www.bmi.bund.de/SharedDocs/downloads/DE/veroeffentlichungen/themen/oeffentlicher-dienst/tarifvertraege/tvoed.html) salary table. DESY offers its employees a financial supplement for a German job ticket (Deutschland-Ticket) at both locations.For further information please contact Dr. Summer Blot at +49 33762-7-7346 (summer.blot@desy.de) or Prof. Dr. Marek Kowalski at +49 33762-7-7187 (marek.kowalski@desy.de).Please submit your complete application documents (letter of motivation and research interests, CV, list of publications, relevant certificates and three letters of references). Please use our online tool for the submission of the letters of reference: Additional application documents (https://www.desy.de/career/additional_application_documents/index_eng.html)We look forward to receiving your application via our application portal:Apply now (https://www.desy.de/career/online_application/index_eng.html?p=18404:10:0&jobid=APPO004/2026&P_LANG=en)DESY promotes equal opportunities, diversity and inclusion (https://www.desy.de/career/working_at_desy/what_we_offer/diversity__inclusion/index_eng.html) . We therefore welcome applications from people of all dimensions of diversity. The professional development of women (https://www.desy.de/career/working_at_desy/what_we_offer/equal_opportunities/index_eng.html) is very important to us and therefore we strongly encourage women to apply for the vacant position. Applications from severely disabled persons and those with equivalent status will be given preference if they are equally qualified (sbv.desy.de) (https://sbv.desy.de/) .You can find further information here:https://www.desy.de/career/ (https://www.desy.de/career/)Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron DESYPersonalabteilungNotkestraße 8522607 HamburgPhone: +49 40 8998-3392

Company:CSR Biotech (www.csr-biotech.eu (http://www.csr-biotech.com/) )Contract:Permanent, Full-time (100%)Location:CSR Biotech Europe Headquarters in Heidelberg, Germany.Company Description:At CSR Biotech, we are committed to advancing the frontiers of scientific and medical innovation.We are growing rapidly in Europe, with our Heidelberg office playing a key role in our global expansion. jobs.employer_name: Technische Universität München (TUM),  Forschungs-Neutronenquelle Heinz Maier-Leibnitz ...
jobs.description: Technical University Munich operates the high flux Neutron Source Heinz Maier-Leibnitz (FRM II) located at the scientific campus in Garching, Germany. The neutron source itself, its research instruments as well as the irradiation facilities provide unique possibilities for the scientific and industrial use of neutron beams.TOFTOF is a neutron time-of-flight chopper spectrometer to study dynamic processes in hard and soft condensed matter. The main areas of application are from materials science, soft matter, biological or magnetic systems. After years of successful operation, the instrument will receive a significant technical upgrade in the coming years.For the further development and the operation of the instrument TOFTOF we invite applications for a full-time (40 h/week) scientist position (m/f/d) asInstrument Scientist Toftof (m/f/d) You will be responsible for the scientific oversight of the technical upgrade of the instrument TOFTOF and attend to its technical realisation.Your tasks include:Scientific lead of TOFTOF’s further developments, i.e. of the neutron transport and chopper system. Conceptual design and future development of the secondary spectrometer, including the neutron detectors. Demonstration of its performance for the intended scientific applications.Project lead for the technical realisation of the upgrade work packages at TOFTOFExperimental tests of instrument critical components to validate performanceMethod development in the area of neutron spectroscopyOperation of the instrument and scientific and technical support in user operationPursuit of own scientific projects using neutron spectroscopy methodsYour responsibility is focused on the instrument TOFTOF. In future, your tasks might include further instrumentation projects.PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, or a related field.Strong background in neutron spectroscopy and hands-on experience with experimental techniques and instrumentation. Experience with polarized neutrons are an asset.Demonstrated ability to conduct instrumentation projects and operate complex scientific setups.Knowledge of scientific programming and data analysis (e.g. Python, C++, MATLAB) is required, experience with ray tracing simulation packages, e.g. McStas, are beneficial.Self-motivated and independent working style combined with the ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary team.Demonstrated ability to conduct independent scientific research and motivation to develop an own scientific research profilePersuasive communication skills and ability to work in a team in an international environment are mandatory. Good oral and written English skills are required, German language skills are an asset.For further information about the position, please contact Wiebke Lohstroh, E-Mail: wiebke.lohstroh@frm2.tum.deThe high safety standard of our facility requires the reliability of the employees according to German nuclear law. Appropriate reliability checks have to be performed for all employees.We offer flexible working hours, 30 days' vacation per year and a company pension plan (VBL). As an employee of FRM II, you can benefit from many other TUM offers, such asTUM's health offersUniversity sportsTUM's internal continuing education and training opportunitiesTUM childcare (subject to availability)Very good accessibility by public transportThe position is remunerated according to TV-L and limited to 3 years. The position is suitable for severely disabled people. Severely disabled applicants will be given preference if they otherwise have essentially the same suitability, qualifications and professional performance. TUM aims to increase the proportion of women. Applications from women are therefore expressly welcomed.
